items.t: — Two public reference pages for a one-carat lab-grown diamond were read live this morning and returned different numbers. CaratRadar, republished 11 August, puts the one-carat average at $711 and states that its figures are asking-price averages drawn from active certified listings across major online retailers, refreshed daily. TheDiamondPrice, carrying an August 2026 date, puts the fair market price of a one-carat round at $650 on an E-to-F, VVS benchmark and says most comparable stones sit between $590 and $760. The gap is $61, or 9.4% on the lower figure, derived by this desk. The two are not in conflict: $711 sits inside the second page's own band, above its $675 midpoint, which is where an offer should sit against an estimate of what stones fetch. This paper carried a third reference, StoneAlgo at $511 dated 7 August, in its wire on 9 August; that page has not been re-read today. The published span for the same stone runs about 39%

items.b: FOUR NUMBERS FOR ONE LAB-GROWN CARAT, TWO OF THEM OURS
items.t: — This paper carries two lab-grown one-carat marks and they are not the same number. The newsroom tape carries $711, the CaratRadar asking-price average read live this morning. The site's tape chip carries $475, the midpoint of the published CVD wholesale band dated 30 July, locked by the build to the lab-grown price list it links to so the chip and the list can never quote two different figures. Both are correct on their own basis and each is footnoted on the page with its quantity and its date. A third figure, $727, was printed on the retail desk panel under the label "Lab-grown 1ct, wholesale" with no source and no date attached and disagreed with our own wholesale midpoint under nearly the same label; it has been taken off the page today and replaced with the sourced $475. Read with the two outside references above, the same stone carries $475, $511, $650, $711 and $727 across five published surfaces, and the only one this desk could not stand behind was its own

— Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time reads gold $4,372.80 an ounce, which is $140.59 a gram and AED 516.31 a gram at the dirham's fixed peg of 3.6725, both conversions this desk's arithmetic. LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 11 August at 10:04 UTC, reads AED 516.26, five fils from the peg figure. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated today, reads AED 526.75. The wedge is AED 10.44, or 2.02% of the metal, against AED 10.66 yesterday and AED 1.08 on 7 August. All three readings moved together overnight, the peg adding AED 3.72, LivePriceOfGold AED 3.81 and Goodreturns AED 3.50, inside AED 0.31 of each other. The AED 13.25 step Goodreturns took between 7 and 8 August was a one-off repricing rather than a page that had stopped updating, and the margin it opened has held through a metal rally

items.b: THE EDITOR'S READ IS THE MARK
items.t: — Under the one-price rule the tape carries this desk's 06:00 New York reading of Kitco's live board on 11 August: gold $4,372.80, silver $64.79, platinum $1,764.00 and palladium $1,362.00. The 04:58 tape had read $4,369.70, $64.60, $1,752.00 and $1,357.00; that is one open session moving between two reads, and the fresher verified reading has been written back with its timestamp and source. Against this paper's own mark of record 24 hours earlier, gold is up $31.40 or 0.72%, silver $0.80 or 1.25%, platinum $27.00 or 1.55% and palladium $22.00 or 1.64%. Those changes measure desk to desk across a day rather than one trading session: Kitco's own session line at the same moment read gold and silver lower against its previous close. Two conventions, one price, and the tape states which it uses. Fine gold $140.59 a gram; the gold-to-silver ratio narrows to 67.49 from 67.84

— Kalyan Jewellers announced on 3 August a second retail brand that will trade in one Indian state and nowhere else. Akshaya Thanga Maligai opens its first showroom at Panagal Park in T. Nagar, Chennai, on 21 August, selling hallmarked gold and certified diamond jewellery cut to Tamil Nadu design preferences, and the group intends to expand it by franchise within the state before considering any other. The actor Sivakarthikeyan has been signed to carry it. Kalyan itself runs more than 400 showrooms across India, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, the United States and the United Kingdom. Franchise capital rather than owned showrooms puts the working capital for the gold on somebody else's balance sheet with spot at $4,372.80 an ounce. The backdrop this paper has filed all month is Indian gold jewellery demand down 15% by weight in the second quarter to 75.1 tonnes and Kalyan taking more than 46% of June-quarter revenue in recycled metal

items.b: THE PULL QUOTE STOPS BEING A QUOTE
items.t: — The standards desk found on 10 August that this paper's pull-quote block set the desk's own analysis inside a quotation element with a speech attribution, on four of that edition's five articles and, on inspection, on all 229 pull quotes this paper has ever published. Not one of them was ever the words of an outside source. The renderer was corrected this morning ahead of the edition and pushed on its own commit: the display line is no longer a quotation element and no longer carries a dash attribution, across every article page on the site. No figure, date or fact was touched and nothing has been altered in any article's text, so this is not a Corrections-block case under the 8 August rule and is recorded here instead. One part of the finding did not survive checking: three passages it reported as quotation-marked body text carry no quotation marks in the served HTML, on the live page or in the build. The single quoted element per article was real and is gone

— Both items on the Bureau's slate were pulled. The Shanghai gold contract settling at 938.80 yuan a gram on 10 August, up 1.33%, was confirmed on source by the Bureau and killed here as a near-repeat: this paper printed 938 yuan for the Shanghai exchange on 9 August and eight tenths of a yuan two days later is not information. The UAE retail figure of 511.5 dirhams a gram, attributed to CNN Business Arabic and unconfirmed by the Bureau on a redirect-blocked fetch, was dropped in favour of this desk's own live reads of the same market. Gem Diamonds' first-half figures, ranked second on the marketing memo's assignment list, were checked and killed: the trading update is dated 28 July and this paper covered it on 29 July as gem-diamonds-rides-the-big-ones, carrying the 52.24-carat stone at $32,908 a carat from the same release. A monthly RapNet figure surfaced in search reporting the 1-carat index down 1.1% on Trump's India tariffs was traced and killed as a date trap: those tariff dates are August 2025, and Rapaport's Diamond Pulse dated 4 August 2026 carries June figures, the 0.30-carat index up 4.2% and the 0.50-carat up 1.3%

items.b: FIVE OF SIX DOMESTIC DESKS DARK
items.t: — The Bureau filed two items today against a usual eight to twelve, both from the overnight Asia and Gulf desk, after every one of the six domestic beats returned a genuine dry day on the same morning for the first time in the log. The cause is shared rather than coincidental: Rapaport and RapNet returning 403 since 5 August, IDEX Online the same, Mining Weekly newly blocked on 9 August, WatchCharts for a sixth consecutive run, Chrono24 behind Cloudflare, and the Brilliant Earth, Pandora and Signet press pages all 403 today after carrying the last two editions' leads. Three articles were filed today rather than eight to ten. A short honest edition beats a padded one, and the Editor's own sweep of the dark beats returned only material already published or unverifiable at source

— Colour has now missed seven consecutive editions, its last appearance being minus-point-one-for-color on 4 August, and it is the paper's longest dark streak on record. The Editor checked the standing anchors directly rather than accepting the beat's file. Gemfields' most recent higher-quality emerald auction is the May sale at $26.8 million and $146.08 a carat, published here on 20 July, with nothing since and the next mixed-quality auction not due until October. The Fancy Color Research Foundation's second-quarter index ran here on 4 August. Its long-run series, which would be new, cannot be printed: the foundation's own index page publishes no figures, the cumulative numbers circulating in search trace only to a lender's marketing blog, and IDEX's report of 5 August carries the quarterly and twelve-month moves but no series since 2005. The marketing memo's first-ranked assignment is a standing colour anchor, and the finding for it today is that FCRF cannot be that anchor because it puts its index behind membership. Diamonds breaks a three-edition dark streak; watches and auctions are dark a second consecutive edition
